correctness.rationale: For the repaired proof, finite reduced even part is a product of finite separable fields by ordinary Artin–Wedderburn and the finite division ring theorem. The finite-dimensional graded radical is the largest nilpotent graded ideal, hence has no even part and squares to zero. Semisimplicity of the neutral enveloping algebra gives a bimodule complement in degree one; odd-odd products land in degree zero. The quotient has no nilpotent graded ideals since their lifts are nilpotent. For each off-diagonal odd corner its two-sided annihilator of the reverse corner is a square-zero graded ideal, because all other odd-odd products vanish by degree and idempotent support. Nonzero reverse pairings therefore occur, can be normalized to opposite idempotents, prohibit two neighbors, and force a neighboring diagonal odd corner to be a square-zero ideal. Matrix units then give the two-vertex block. At an isolated field vertex the annihilator is again a square-zero ideal; every nonzero odd element has an inverse. Conjugation has order dividing two, and the bijective square map or surjective quadratic norm removes the square twist. The map a+b u to a+b sigma is faithful by evaluation at 1 and at an element moved by sigma. The external even unit gives a reduced neutral unitization; its graded radical equals the original one by nilpotence and scalar action. The complement intersected with A is a graded ideal of a product of unital graded-simple factors and splits along their even identities. The supplied finite matrix checker was inspected only; the universal argument is algebraic.

evidence: Graded Artin–Wedderburn classifies the already graded-semisimple components as graded endomorphism rings. Homogeneous components of a graded-division ring are generated by invertible homogeneous elements, giving crossed products.

value.rationale: The criterion replaces a base-field polynomial identity with an intrinsic condition that allows all finite neutral field extensions, yet gives a graded complement even in the modular characteristic. It identifies the sole additional form of graded-simple block needed in this scope and separates the radical at the level of the full algebra, not just the quotient or a single M2 example.
